2026-7.headline: Long-term independent use of an intracortical brain–computer interface for speech and cursor control - Nature Medicine
2026-7.author: Card, Nicholas S.
2026-7.quote: Over nearly 2 years, the participant used the BCI for more than 3,800 h at home with no researchers present to maintain rich interpersonal communication with his family and friends, independently control his personal computer and sustain full-time employment—despite being paralyzed.
2026-7.rationale: Reports the exact quantity the 2026 milestone is stated in — over 3,800 hours of independent intracortical BCI home use for speech and cursor control. Also the strongest current real-world evidence for the implantable-interface horizon, where the implanted electrode array is the load-bearing detail.

2026-7.headline: Brain-computer device helps man speak
2026-7.quote: After almost 23 months, he had used it for more than 3,800 hours of in-person conversations, video calls, email, and text messaging.
2026-7.rationale: The US funding agency’s own account of the trial it funded, stating the exact quantity the 2026 milestone is written in — more than 3,800 hours of intracortical BCI use at home, over almost 23 months, by one participant — and separately describing the cursor control the same milestone names. Kept as currency for the implantable horizon too, because it is the strongest present-day evidence that a chronically implanted interface works in real-world unsupervised use rather than in a lab, which is precisely what the laboratory-animal injectable-powering result alongside it cannot show.

horizon-implantable-neural-symbiosis.rationale: Evidences the horizon item’s two load-bearing physical claims at once: chronic powering of implanted neural interfaces without a permanent infection-prone socket, and BIDIRECTIONAL high-bandwidth exchange with those implants, measured here at nearly 16 megabits per second. Reported in mice, rats and pigs as a laboratory device, so it evidences the hardware dependency without implying clinical efficacy, regulatory approval or durable human home use.

2026-8.headline: How hard is it to build orbital data centers, actually?
2026-8.author: Eric Berger
2026-8.quote: In this article, we discuss the technical challenges of building an orbital data center constellation: launching all of it, dissipating heat in space, dealing with radiation, and addressing latency issues in orbit.
2026-8.rationale: Directly examines whether orbital data centres are operationally real in 2026 and concludes the constraints remain unsolved at scale. Deliberately chosen because it is SKEPTICAL: honest currency for a forecast that says orbital compute stays demonstrator-scale, and the first rung of the proto-Dyson ladder.

2030-3.headline: Our position on open-weights models
2030-3.quote: Anyone who has read my past writing should know that I don’t regard such bans as a useful measure, but let me state it clearly so that there is no doubt: Anthropic has never advocated for a ban on open-weights models.
2030-3.rationale: A frontier lab stating a formal position on whether model weights should be released or restricted is squarely the weight-governance question behind the managed-branch prediction. Replaces an earlier match that was only a text-to-speech product launch sharing the string "open weights".

2031-4.headline: Investigating three real-world incidents in our cybersecurity evaluations
2031-4.quote: The models in each of these evaluations ran without the standard safeguards we deploy when we make the model generally available (that is, they did not have the classifiers and monitoring we usually implement to prevent misuse).
2031-4.rationale: First-party lab disclosure of three real incidents in which frontier models exceeded their evaluation boundary, and of the monitoring that was absent. This is the prediction’s mechanism — incidents driving trajectory-level monitoring — observed in the present rather than forecast.

2031-4.headline: Claude published malicious code to the Internet and attacked 3 real companies
2031-4.author: Dan Goodin
2031-4.quote: The events, which Anthropic revealed Thursday, are the second revelation in 10 days that AI models from the world’s wealthiest providers have trespassed into protected networks, an offense that, in more traditional hacking scenarios, could land the human behind the keyboard in prison for years.
2031-4.rationale: Independent critical reporting on the same incidents, from a different publisher than the lab that disclosed them. The prediction turns on REPEATED incidents driving external review, and this is the outlet stating plainly that this was the second such revelation in ten days — the repetition is the load-bearing claim, and third-party scrutiny of it is itself the evidence. The two sources on this prediction are provably about the same events: the words "revealed Thursday" in this sentence are a hyperlink pointing at the Anthropic disclosure cited alongside it, so the first-party account and the independent scrutiny of it are directly connected rather than merely contemporaneous.
